sources.entry: Lockpaw by Erik Nielsen - A native-Swift macOS menu-bar app (10 MB, no Electron) that covers and input-locks your screen with one hotkey while your agents keep running, then makes the locked screen glow when Claude Code pauses for permission or finishes. Polished and well-engineered — CI with 50 tests, signed/notarized builds, an honest "visual privacy tool, not a security boundary" disclosure, no

summary.one_liner: Lockpaw is a native-Swift macOS menu-bar app that covers the screen and blocks input with one hotkey while processes keep running, and can glow the locked screen when AI coding agents need attention.
summary.what_it_does: Pressing ⌘⇧L (configurable) covers every connected display with an overlay at the highest system window level and blocks keyboard, scroll and trackpad-gesture input, while builds, downloads, SSH sessions and agents keep running. Unlock is by Touch ID (armed behind the overlay) or a password field on the lock screen checked against the login password, with a 30-second cooldown after 3 failed attempts. When Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot or Aider pause for permission or finish, the locked screen glows and a notification names the agent and project. Optional features include a lid-closed mode via a root LaunchDaemon that sets pmset disablesleep, forwarding pings to ntfy, Pushover or a webhook, a lockpaw CLI with install-hook commands for each agent, and lockpaw:// URL scheme actions. The README describes it as a visual privacy tool rather than a security boundary.
use_cases: hide my screen while agents or builds keep running
get notified when Claude Code or Codex needs permission
cover screen at work without sleeping the Mac
keep AI coding agents running with the laptop lid closed
send agent alerts to phone via ntfy or Pushover
lock screen from Shortcuts or a URL scheme
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd lockpaw && xcodegen generate
notable: Lid-closed mode uses an opt-in root LaunchDaemon whose XPC interface is a single sleep on/off switch, with mutual code-signature checks
Agent alerts glow the locked screen amber when waiting and teal when done, with a CLI that wires hooks into each agent's config and keeps .bak backups
Input tap also intercepts Dock gesture events so three-finger Space swipes are blocked
Explicit security model listing what it does not protect against, such as pkill and synthetic events
caveats: Visual privacy tool, not a security boundary; pkill Lockpaw and synthetic events are not blocked
Requires Accessibility permission and macOS-specific APIs; macOS only
Lid-closed mode needs a one-time helper approval and changes pmset sleep behavior
